newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria govt partner surprised by resignation.
newsitem.headline: Austria govt partner surprised by resignation.

text.p: Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel expressed surprise on Saturday over Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's resignation and said he been told just an hour before it was officially announced.
Schuessel, who leads the conservative People's Party, the junior partner in Vranitzky's Social Democrat-led government, immediately called for an urgent round of coalition talks.

"He did not inform us ahead of time as would have been customary," a clearly irritated Schuessel told Austrian television. "I was in Switzerland the whole day in my role as foreign minister, but would have been contactable at any time."
Vranitzky said he would step down as chancellor and head of the Social Democrats after almost 11 years at the helm of government, hinting he had become tired with politics.
Schuessel said he had received a phone call by Vranitzky barely an hour before he went public with his resignation.
The People's Party and the Social Democrats have ruled in an uneasy coalition for nearly 10 years and renewed their partnership after a snap general election in December 1995.

The coalition survived its most precarious crisis last weekend when Finance Minister Viktor Klima, Vranitzky's designated successor, sealed the sale of conservative bank Creditanstalt to rival Bank Austria against strong opposition by the People's Party.
Schuessel indicated his party was willing to continue their partnership with Klima, but said the two camps had to start negotiations immediately.

"For us it is important that we continue our work on the basis of the existing coalition agreement. We want to take part in the decision-making process. We want a very concrete set of talks," he said.
President Thomas Klestil accepted Vranitzky's resignation, but asked him to stay on in a caretaker position until Klima had presented his new cabinet line-up.
Constitutionally, the entire cabinet has to be sworn in anew alongside the new chancellor.
The president advised Klima to present his new government within days rather than weeks.

The Social Democrats and the conservatives have almost completely dominated Austria's post-World War Two politics. Despite rumours to the contrary, Schuessel has repeatedly said he has no intention of going into coalition with the far-right Freedom Party led by Joerg Haider.
